channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: Vietnam's industrial production index rose 12.4% year on year in the first ten months of 2026, a record for the period since 2019, with manufacturing and processing up 13.0% and motor vehicle manufacturing up 14.6%.
item.description:
The Vietnam Economic Times reports, citing the National Statistics Office, that the index of industrial production rose 12.4% year on year in the first ten months of 2026, a record for the corresponding period of 2019 to 2026. Manufacturing and processing grew 13.0% and contributed 10.2 percentage points of the increase, mining grew 7.1%, electricity production and distribution 10.6%, and water supply, waste management and wastewater treatment 9.2%. Metal production rose 25.6%, beverage manufacturing 17.5%, computer, electronic and optical products 15.2% and motor vehicle manufacturing 14.6%, while leather and related products grew 4.3% and hard and brown coal mining fell 0.6%. VietnamPlus, citing the Ministry of Industry and Trade, reports that total trade in the ten months was estimated at USD 1.01 trillion, up 32.3% year on year, and exports at USD 499 billion, up 27.4%. The rows do not give output in volume terms, a breakdown by foreign-invested and domestic companies or the destination of the exports.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report growth rates of an index and estimates of trade values, not volumes of chemicals or materials. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, double-digit growth in manufacturing and in exports describes a manufacturing base that is expanding quickly, and growth in metals, electronics and vehicles points to demand from industries that use industrial materials. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, such growth could support demand for bonding, sealing and coating materials in Vietnam, while the rows give no figures for materials. Points that may be worth considering include Vietnam's November data, the outcome of the US investigation and the sources of Vietnam's imported inputs.

Vietnam Economic Times | VietnamPlus

item.title: OECD input-output analysis finds China accounted for about 37–47% of world value added in five manufacturing industries in 2024, against 2000, when no economy exceeded 28% in any manufacturing industry.
item.description:
The OECD publication on economic security in global production, based on its Inter-Country Input-Output (ICIO) analysis, reports significant shifts in global manufacturing over two decades. While no individual economy accounted for more than 28% of world value added in any manufacturing industry in 2000, by 2024 China accounted for approximately 37–47% in five industries. The analysis says these changes have also reshaped international supplier relationships: China's position as the largest foreign source of value added in country-industry final demand relationships increased from around 4% in 2000 to 40% in 2024, with a large margin to the next supplier. The row does not name the five industries, define the 40% measure or the countries whose final demand is meant, or give figures for any other economy.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row reports shares of value added from one model, not trade flows or prices. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a share of 37–47% of world value added in five industries describes concentration of production in one country, which is the kind of concentration that economic security policies target, while the row does not define the 40% measure, so it cannot be read as showing how many buyers lack an alternative. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, if the five industries include chemicals or other materials, or the customers' industries such as machinery or electronics, the concentration would affect sourcing, while the row does not say which industries are meant. Points that may be worth considering include the OECD's list of the five industries, the measure behind the 40% and trade-defence or sourcing measures by the EU and the US.

OECD

item.title: The US trade representative's intellectual property investigation of Vietnam is due to be completed on 29 November; Tesla and Samsung oppose new duties, while US steel, seafood, solar and wood groups want stronger action.
item.description:
Commercial Times reports that the Office of the United States Trade Representative plans to complete on 29 November its investigation into intellectual property rights in Vietnam, launched in May. Vietnam is listed as a Priority Foreign Country, the first country in 13 years on the highest-level watch list; the US accuses Vietnam of a "long-term failure to address intellectual property protection and enforcement issues". A uniform 12.5% US tariff has applied to Vietnamese goods since July, imposed after another investigation showed that Vietnam failed to prevent imports of goods made with forced labour. Business Standard, citing Reuters, reports that companies such as Samsung and Tesla oppose additional duties and that companies with manufacturing operations in Vietnam warned in submissions to the US government that additional tariffs could disrupt their supply chains, while groups representing US producers of steel, seafood, solar panels and other products want penalties; LiveMint lists steel, seafood, solar, wood and software groups. The rows do not say whether new tariffs would apply generally or to specific industries, at what rate, or from when.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report an investigation with a deadline and company submissions, not a decision. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, duties that follow the investigation would add to the 12.5% tariff and raise the cost of goods made in Vietnam, and the companies' warnings point to supply chains that run through the country. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, Vietnam is a manufacturing location for electronics and other goods in which adhesives and coatings are used, so tariffs could change production and sourcing decisions, while the rows give no figures for these industries. Points that may be worth considering include the outcome of the investigation due to be completed on 29 November, the scope and rate of any measure, and the response of Vietnam.

Commercial Times | Business Standard | LiveMint

item.title: Italian new car registrations rose 4.8% in October to 131,921, an eleventh consecutive positive monthly result against a reported 9.9% in September, and are 16.1% below October 2019, La Repubblica (citing Unrae) and ANSA report.
item.description:
La Repubblica reports Unrae data showing 131,921 new car registrations in Italy in October 2026 against 125,864 in October 2025, up 4.8%, and 1,400,991 in the first ten months of 2026, up 8.3% from 1,293,406. Rechargeable vehicles were 18.8% of registrations in October, pure electric cars 6.1% and plug-in hybrids 12.7%. ANSA calls it the eleventh consecutive positive monthly result, at a pace below the 9.9% it reports for September, a base the row does not state, and reports that the market is 16.1% below October 2019 and 13.8% below the January to October period of 2019. The rows do not give registrations by brand, working-day effects or production figures.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report registrations, which measure sales, not vehicle production. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, growth of 4.8% in October against the 9.9% ANSA reports for September, a base the row does not state, while the level stays well below 2019 describes a market that is recovering but has not recovered, and registrations feed through to carmakers' and suppliers' order books with a lag. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, vehicle assembly uses bonding, sealing and coating materials in bodies, interiors and battery systems, so production volumes matter more than registrations in one country, and the rows give no production or materials data. Points that may be worth considering include Italian production data, registrations in Germany and France, and the electrified share of registrations.

La Repubblica | ANSA

item.title: ADNOC's chief executive says global oil inventories fell by almost 1 billion barrels after Hormuz shipping was disrupted, and shipping and logistics costs rose to 30% of the cost per barrel from 5%.
item.description:
Pakistan Today and China Economic Net report remarks on 2 November by Sultan Al Jaber, chief executive of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC). Global oil inventories have fallen by almost 1 billion barrels since shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted by the US-Israeli war on Iran, which, in Pakistan Today's wording, significantly reduces supply buffers as fuel prices and transport costs increase. Diesel inventories in some regions had fallen to their lowest levels for this time of year in 35 years, according to Pakistan Today, while China Economic Net gives the lowest level in 35 years without the seasonal qualifier and 1 billion barrels for the fall in inventories; other markets were facing a shortfall in liquefied natural gas supply of 600 billion cubic feet, or 16.99 billion cubic metres in the Chinese row. Al Jaber said shipping and logistics costs have risen to 30% of the cost per barrel of oil, from 5% before the conflict. The Los Angeles Times, citing the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), reports that the average US diesel price rose almost 67% from just before the war began on 28 February to 26 October. The rows do not say which regions have the low diesel stocks, which stocks the 1 billion barrels cover, or the basis for the 30% share.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report one executive's figures and one price series, not an independent inventory count. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, lower inventories leave less supply to absorb disruptions, so prices can react more strongly to news, and, if the executive's 30% share for shipping and logistics is accurate, transport has become a large part of the cost per barrel. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, diesel and other oil products set transport and energy costs along the supply chain, and petrochemical raw materials follow crude with a lag, so low stocks could keep these costs high for longer, while the rows give no figures for chemical raw materials. Points that may be worth considering include official inventory data from the EIA and the IEA, diesel prices in Europe and freight quotes for tankers.

Pakistan Today | China Economic Net | Los Angeles Times

item.title: The US ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5, against 54.6 expected, with the production index up 2.3 points to 59, the highest since November 2021, and input prices at 75.2.
item.description:
The Institute for Supply Management reports that its US manufacturing purchasing managers' index rose from 54.5 in September to 55.5 in October, higher than the 54.6 the market expected according to Commercial Times; Cnyes calls it the second-highest reading in more than four years. The production index rose 2.3 points to 59, the highest since November 2021, MarketScreener reports, and Cnyes reports the new orders index at 55.5, up from 55.3, with factory inventories and export orders also higher. Twelve industries reported growth, among them transportation equipment, electrical equipment, appliances and components, machinery, primary metals, textile mills and computer and electronic products, and three reported contraction: paper products, printing and related support activities, and nonmetallic mineral products. The Economic Times reports that factory input prices stayed elevated at 75.2, that some manufacturers complained that economic policies coming out of Washington continue to weigh on business conditions and that a recent escalation in the trade war with Canada was also cited as a constraint, and that economists cautioned that rising interest rates and falling inflation-adjusted household income would hamper manufacturing next year, especially in segments not exposed to AI spending. The rows do not give the index by company size or region or output in volume terms.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report a survey index of purchasing managers, not production volumes. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a production index at 59, the highest since late 2021, describes expanding factory activity, while input prices at 75.2 are described as still elevated. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, transportation equipment, machinery, electrical equipment and appliances are customers for bonding, sealing and coating materials, so a broad expansion in these industries could support demand, while contraction in nonmetallic mineral products points the other way. Points that may be worth considering include the November index, its new orders and input price components, and US industrial production data.

Cnyes.com | Commercial Times | MarketScreener | The Economic Times

item.title: The scientific advisory board to Germany's economy ministry says the housing shortage slows growth because high housing costs make it harder to move to a more productive job, Süddeutsche Zeitung and Tagesschau report.
item.description:
Süddeutsche Zeitung and Tagesschau report on an expert report by the scientific advisory board to the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, headed by Minister Katherina Reiche (CDU). The advisers say the housing shortage slows growth: high housing costs burden households and make it difficult to move to a more productive job, so a person who cannot find affordable housing near a better-paid job cannot take it, according to board chairman Felix Bierbrauer. Tagesschau adds that high rents slow the mobility of workers and can stop companies attracting specialists, and that the problem is most visible in economically strong regions, where wages are often higher, but so are rents. The Süddeutsche Zeitung text adds that creating more housing in growth regions is therefore a central task of economic policy. In a separate release the Bundesingenieurkammer reports that it and 29 other organisations, including associations of the construction and real estate industry, the trade union IG BAU and the German Tenants' Association, warn that the government's planned reduction in housing subsidies would further cripple housing construction, on the occasion of the adjustment meeting for the 2027 federal budget, and cite an ifo Institute forecast of a new record low of only 185,000 new homes for the current year. The rows do not give the size of the planned subsidy reduction, the date of the budget meeting, any figures from the advisory board or its recommendations beyond more housing in growth regions.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report an advisory board's assessment and an alliance's warning, apart from one ifo forecast, not data on construction activity or a decided budget. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a housing shortage that weighs on growth gives the government a reason to support construction, while a planned reduction in housing subsidies points the other way, so the direction of policy for 2027 is open. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, German residential construction and renovation use bonding, sealing and coating materials, so the budget decision could affect volumes in this end market, while the rows give no figures for materials. Points that may be worth considering include the outcome of the budget adjustment meeting, the size of the planned housing subsidy reduction and German building permits.

Süddeutsche Zeitung | Tagesschau | Bundesingenieurkammer

item.title: US construction spending fell 1.9% in September from the revised August estimate to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of USD 2,186.1 billion, 2.7% below September 2025, according to Census Bureau estimates.
item.description:
The American Bankers Association, citing the Census Bureau, reports that construction spending in September was at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of USD 2,186.1 billion, 1.9% below the revised August estimate of USD 2,227.4 billion and 2.7% below the September 2025 estimate of USD 2,245.8 billion. In the first nine months of the year spending was USD 1,649.6 billion, 2.9% below USD 1,698.6 billion in the same period of 2025. MarketScreener reports that the annualised pace of private construction fell 2.4% to USD 1.639 trillion and residential construction fell 5.5% to USD 848.8 billion, while public-sector spending fell 0.1% to USD 546.8 billion, spending on schools was flat at USD 113.1 billion and highway construction fell 0.3% to USD 149.2 billion. The rows do not state the comparison period of the changes MarketScreener gives for private, residential, public, school and highway spending, nor spending on private non-residential buildings, price adjustments, revisions to earlier months or an explanation for the fall.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report dollar spending, not building volumes or permits. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a fall in the month together with a decline against the same month and the same period of last year describes a market below last year's level, while residential spending is reported down 5.5% and public-sector spending down 0.1% with no comparison period given for either. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, construction spending is a broad indicator for the volumes of bonding, sealing and coating materials used in new buildings and civil works, while the rows give no figures for materials and the dollar value moves with prices. Points that may be worth considering include the October release, US housing starts and permits, and non-residential spending.

American Bankers Association | MarketScreener

item.title: More than 40 German associations, including BDI, VCI and VDMA, asked the Chancellery on 29 October to halt a plastic tax that a preliminary draft sets at EUR 550 per tonne of plastic in packaging from July 2027, Handelsblatt and Yahoo Germany report.
item.description:
Handelsblatt reports that more than 40 business associations protest in a letter to the Chancellery against a planned plastic tax. They include the Federation of German Industries (BDI), the German Retail Federation, the Association of German Chambers of Commerce and Industry (DIHK), the chemical industry association VCI, the engineering federation VDMA, the electrical industry association ZVEI and the confectionery industry federation. Yahoo Germany reports that the letter was submitted on 29 October by 42 associations. They warn that the tax would increase bureaucracy, create competitive disadvantages and make everyday products more expensive, would add expenditure for public administration and would not create investment incentives for more sustainable packaging or additional recycling capacity. A preliminary draft would charge EUR 550 for every tonne of plastic in packaging from July 2027. Yahoo Germany reports that the government is wrangling over the tax, that the SPD is pushing the project while the Union has strong reservations, and that Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) plans to use the revenue, expected at EUR 805 million in 2027 and nearly EUR 1.5 billion a year from 2028. The rows do not give the draft's treatment of recycled plastic or exemptions, a date for a cabinet decision or a response from the Chancellery.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report a draft rate and an industry letter, not an adopted law. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a levy charged per tonne of plastic in packaging makes plastic packaging dearer against other materials and can shift packaging choices, and a levy still disputed in the government may stay uncertain for companies that plan packaging for 2027. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, adhesives and coatings are used in flexible and rigid plastic packaging and in laminates, and a change in the mix of plastic and other materials could change the bonding and sealing tasks, while the rows give no figures on this. Points that may be worth considering include a cabinet draft and its start date, any exemption for recycled content, and the positions of the Union and the SPD.

Handelsblatt | Yahoo! Germany

item.title: Oil prices fell more than 6% at one point on 2 November on optimism over US-Iran talks; Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions, and Trump says a deal "could happen".
item.description:
Asharq Al-Awsat reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions as efforts escalated to avert a return to war. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said indirect talks were taking place through mediators, and The Standard adds that Iran said "intensive" exchanges with the US were under way and that in September Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait if the US agreed to a list of demands. China urged a return to negotiations, and Iran's security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Commercial Times reports that Iran's supreme leader approved the government starting negotiations to resolve the conflict, that Iranian and Qatari officials held talks for a third consecutive day, and that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump aims to resolve the conflict through diplomatic channels, while other reports indicated that both sides were preparing for possible further strikes after the midterm elections. Arab News reports Trump saying a deal "could happen". Asharq Al-Awsat reports oil prices dropped more than 6% on Monday, Commercial Times reports a fall of more than 6% at one point and, in a later report, of nearly 4%, and the Economic Times reports that Brent fell and the S&P 500 energy index fell 4%. The Hindu BusinessLine, in an earlier report on the same day, put the decline in oil prices at over 1%, and adds that Brent ended October at its highest level in six months amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again after the election. The rows do not state the conditions Iran attaches, a date for any reopening, the closing level of Brent, the size of the move at the close or which benchmark and time each figure refers to.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report an offer and talks, not an agreement, and a one-day move in oil prices, not a change in the flow of oil through the strait. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a conditional offer for which the rows report no acceptance leaves open whether flows recover, and a price that falls on hopes of a deal can reverse if talks stall, as the reports of preparations for strikes after the election indicate. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, crude and its products set the cost of many raw materials with a lag, so a lasting fall in oil prices could ease raw material costs, while the rows give no price for resins, solvents or freight. Points that may be worth considering include the conditions Iran attaches, any US reply, Brent after the 3 November election and shipping data for the strait.

Asharq Al-Awsat | The Standard | Commercial Times | Commercial Times | Arab News | The Hindu BusinessLine | The Economic Times

item.title: A Rhodium Group report for the US Chamber of Commerce finds China almost doubled its chemicals capacity in some areas in five years and makes about half of global output of certain products, the Financial Times reports.
item.description:
The Financial Times reports on a report compiled by Rhodium Group on behalf of the US Chamber of Commerce. It finds that in five years China has almost doubled its chemicals capacity in some areas and now accounts for about half of the global output of certain products. Chinese producers are displacing foreign producers across many different production and supply chain channels and are outcompeting incumbents in the faster-growing emerging markets, according to the report. Over the five-year period, exports of four petrochemical products, excluding ethylene, grew by an average of more than 40% each year. The row does not name the products or the areas where capacity almost doubled, does not give capacity, output or export volumes, does not say which five years are covered or which emerging markets are meant, and gives no prices or any view from Chinese producers.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row reports headline findings of one study, not capacity or trade data. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, capacity that has almost doubled in some areas, together with average export growth of more than 40% a year in four petrochemical products, describes supply that may look for buyers abroad, and producers outside China may meet it first in emerging markets. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, petrochemical products are the starting point for many resins, polymers and solvents, so growth in Chinese capacity and exports could affect the price and availability of raw materials, while the row does not say which products are involved. Points that may be worth considering include the full report's list of products and areas, Chinese export volumes and prices for products used as raw materials, and trade-defence actions in the markets that receive the exports.

The Financial Times
